subject: SDK Onramp: Local dev plan & sample app checklist
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@fathominc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: SDK Onramp: Local dev plan & sample app checklist

Hi Samir / Alyssa —

Great call today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and a proposed minimal onramp so your engineers can validate the integration locally this week:

1) Repo & quickstart
   - We have a small sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/tree/brightlane-onramp (attached zip is a trimmed copy).
   - Checkout the "python-basic" and "ts-basic" folders for two runnable examples.

2) Auth & env
   - Create an API key in the Redwood Console (or we can mint a scoped key for you).
   - Local env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION (recommend us-east1), REDWOOD_MODEL (start with "redwood-medium").

3) Install & run (local)
   - Python: pip install redwood-sdk && python examples/python-basic/run_local.py
   - TypeScript: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk && npm run start --prefix examples/ts-basic

4) Routing & model variants
   - For your low-latency UI paths use the dedicated endpoint in us-east1. We recommend the medium variant for cost/latency balance; switch to small for quick smoke runs.

5) Structured output / tool-calling
   - Both samples include a function-calling example (tools/router and tools/db_lookup). We show a schema-based JSON response to make client parsing deterministic.

6) Embeddings & reranker
   - Embeddings endpoint and a basic reranker script included: examples/embeddings/encode.py and examples/rerank/quick_rerank.ts.
   - Default vector dim is 1536; store locally for the pilot or configure your vector DB (we include a SQLite example).

7) Local test checklist
   - Confirm outbound access to api.redwood.ai:443 (or let us provide an internal proxy if your network blocks outbound).
   - Run the python sample and validate: generates sample tokens, embeddings, and a rerank result.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart-stub.zip (zip) — minimal samples + README

Questions for you:
- Can we get an engineer with access to a test laptop this week to try the python sample?
- Any firewall constraints (outbound IP restrictions) or policy for storing embeddings we should be aware of?

Suggested next step: 30-min pairing session — I can share my screen and walk through the repo; propose Tue or Wed morning (PDT).

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — this is helpful. A few quick notes: 

- Wed morning (PDT) works for our eng (we'll confirm exact person).
- Firewall: we have strict egress rules — only whitelisted IPs and an outbound proxy. Can you provide the hostname/IP range your SDK needs to reach?
- Embeddings retention: our security team flags storing embeddings in plain DBs. We'll likely want to encrypt at rest and have a retention policy. Can you confirm if Redwood stores anything server-side for the hosted flow?

I'll try to run the python sample tomorrow. If I hit errors I'll forward logs. Appreciate the pairing session — Alyssa will join for the architecture-level questions.

—Samir
